Declare and initialize variables upfront: Always define your variables at the beginning of functions or scopes to avoid hoisting surprises and improve readability.
Create modular, specialized functions: Break down large functions into smaller, single-purpose ones that handle one task well, promoting reusability.
DRY Principle: Eliminate duplicate code: Refactor repeated logic into shared functions or utilities to reduce maintenance overhead and bugs.
DRY: Don't Repeat Yourself: Extract common code into functions or classes to minimize duplication.
YAGNI: Avoid premature features: Build only what's needed now to prevent over-engineering.
KISS: Keep It Simple: Favor straightforward solutions over complex ones for easier maintenance.
Write unit tests first (TDD): Define behavior via tests before implementation for robust coverage.
Refactor regularly: Improve code structure without changing behavior to curb tech debt.
Design before coding: Sketch architecture and interfaces to avoid integration pitfalls.
Anticipate requirements changes: Build flexible architectures with loose coupling.
Defensive programming: Validate assumptions and inputs to prevent crashes.
Use intention-revealing names: Choose variables/functions that describe their purpose clearly.
Read others' code daily: Study open-source for style and patterns to evolve yours.
